report: Cross-verse: all nine candidate groups are context differences, not splits. לְ is unrepresented in v1, v5 and v6 because the ASV recasts each dative suffix as a bare 'me'/'my'/'her' (rule 40) and takes 'unto' in v3 and 'are for' in v7 where a word is written for it (rules 11, 49). לָשׁוֹן רְמִיָּה is rendered attributively in both v2 and v3, with the supplied 'a' (rule 29) and the vocative 'Thou' (rule 36) each on the construct noun. שָׁכַן takes a bare 'I dwell' in v5 and the light-verb 'hath had dwelling' headed on 'dwelling' in v6 (rule 44; PRO.8.12 heads the same rendering the same way). שָׁלוֹם takes 'am for peace' as nominal predicate in v7 (rules 20, 33; ECC.3.8 gives 'for peace' to the bare noun) and bare 'peace' as object in v6.

The one genuinely hedged unit is v5's second 'That', read as the distributed realization of the single כִּי over the asyndetic second colon (rules 25/55); the note names the added-under-55 alternative. No patch: the reading is defensible and consistent with rule 25's asyndetic-colon sentence.
BSB disagreements (2 paragogic he, 3 dative לְ) are the documented convention differences of rules 32 and 40; none is an error.
No convention recorded: the repeated 'Rectum rendered attributively (rule 28)' note restates the contract. No promotion: the chapter taught nothing the contract lacks.
